description: REST / RPC APIs and HTTP methods as developers write them: CRUD tables, nested resources, versioned APIs, method-agnostic middleware and findAllRoutes ordering
sources: README: Route patterns (Params, Wildcards, Groups), Matching (Methods and paths, Routes for any method, Trailing slashes and empty segments, Path normalization, Result ordering incl. carve-outs)
.agents/matching.md: same-node siblings, method-agnostic entries, findAllRoutes ordering
GitHub REST API v3 route shapes (docs.github.com/rest), Stripe API v1 route shapes (docs.stripe.com/api)
Google AIP-136 custom methods (`/books/{id}:archive`), tRPC / Connect / Twirp / JSON-RPC URL shapes

scenarios.name: users resource with numeric ids and an admin guard
Rails-style posts resource (index/new/create/show/edit/update/destroy)
scenarios.description: The seven RESTful actions on one resource: static `new` beats `:id`, and `/posts/new/edit` backtracks to `:id`

scenarios.name: GitHub-like REST API slice (35 routes)
scenarios.description: Nested owner/repo resources, numeric issue numbers, static siblings of params (`releases/latest`, `issues/comments`), `:path*` contents, `**:ref` git refs, `:base...:head` compare, and a method-agnostic repo-access middleware

scenarios.name: Stripe-like API v1 with API-key middleware
scenarios.description: `search` / `upcoming` static siblings of `:id`, a prefixed-id route `cus_:id` beside `:id`, POST-to-update and action sub-resources

cases.note: no POST search route: the param route takes it

scenarios.name: versioned APIs (`/v:version(\d+)`, `:version(v1|v2)`, optional version groups)
regex constraint classes: slugs, hex ids, compare ranges
scenarios.description: README Invalid patterns: a `--` / `&&` inside a class is a set operation in URLPattern (`v` flag) and throws; a `-` in a class, `--` as literal text and escaped `\-` stay valid

scenarios.name: method-specific vs method-agnostic routes on the same paths
scenarios.description: README 'Routes for any method': equally specific → the method's own route wins (and comes after the `""` one); more specific `""` routes beat less specific method routes; HEAD is not GET; method strings are case-sensitive

cases.note: lowercase is just another method string: only `""` routes see it
the deeper `""` route beats the OPTIONS catch-all

scenarios.name: HEAD and GET registered separately
scenarios.description: rou3 never maps HEAD to GET: a framework must register HEAD or fall back itself

scenarios.name: middleware stack: logger, auth, rate-limit, handler
scenarios.description: README 'Result ordering': findAllRoutes lists `/**` < `/api/**` < `/api/users/**` < handler, so merging the results lets the handler win

scenarios.name: catch-all flavours on one node: `**` < `*` < `**:name`
scenarios.description: README detailed ordering: on a shared node a `**` comes before a trailing `*` (same paths), before a `**:name` (needs a value); ties keep registration order with `""` first

scenarios.name: registration order breaks exact ties only
scenarios.description: Same node, same weight: findRoute picks the first-registered, findAllRoutes keeps registration order; a `""` route sorts before the method's on a tie whatever the order; a constraint outranks them all

scenarios.name: static siblings of params: `/users/me`, `/new`, `/search` vs `/:slug`
scenarios.description: Static beats param at each level, with backtracking when the static branch has no continuation

scenarios.name: action sub-resources and AIP-136 custom methods
scenarios.description: `/orders/:id/cancel`-style actions and Google-style `/books/:id\:archive` custom verbs beside the plain resource

scenarios.name: files with names and extensions
scenarios.description: `:name.:ext` (lazy name), a fixed `.json` extension, `*.zip` downloads at any depth, and a static-asset `**` fallback

cases.note: containment: `:name` ⊋ `:name.:ext` ⊋ `:name.json` (on their shared node, more literal text ranks higher)

scenarios.name: extension routes registered broadest first
scenarios.description: The same three file routes as above in the order a developer adds them (generic first): the more literal `:name.json` should still win on `data.json`

cases.note: `:name.json` has more literal text than `:name.:ext`: it wins in either registration order

scenarios.name: mounted sub-routers: per-version and per-prefix middleware
scenarios.description: `app.use("/api/:version", …)` and `app.use("/api/v1", …)`-style middleware: the param scope lists before the static one at the same depth, both before the handler

scenarios.name: CORS preflight with OPTIONS and a method-agnostic CORS header middleware

cases.note: the deeper `""` route wins over the root OPTIONS catch-all

scenarios.name: optional format suffix, pagination and optional trailing params

cases.note: README carve-out A1: the broader pattern comes last

scenarios.name: RPC-style endpoints: JSON-RPC, tRPC, Twirp, Connect / gRPC-web
format suffix catch-all ranked from the end (`/**.json` vs `/api/users/:id`)
scenarios.description: README 'Segments after a catch-all': on paths a suffix route matches, results rank from the last segment backwards, so `*.json` beats a plain `:id` there

scenarios.name: README carve-out B: `:name+` before a param and a catch-all
scenarios.description: `/p/:id/**` contains `/p/:path+` but wildcards list first, so the narrower route comes first and findRoute picks the broader

scenarios.name: API gateway / proxy with `**:path` forwarding
admin area behind a `*` guard, with path traversal attempts
scenarios.description: `use("/admin/*")`-style guard covers `/admin` and every depth below; `..` only resolves with `normalize`
